data.description:
## Summary

When the Gerrit edge fails a checkout, CI reports the change as **failing its tests**. A transport
fault and a test verdict are the same signal today, so an infrastructure problem is attributed to
the author's code.

This was AC4 of `antihuman-beefwitted-zebra` (5bba-45dd-3bfc-42f1). That ticket fixed the *cause* of
one such outage (an nginx `proxy_read_timeout` of 60s on the Gerrit block, now 600s). This ticket is
the **signal-quality half**: the next transport fault, from any cause, will still be mislabelled.
Splitting it out because it is a genuinely separate deliverable in different files, and leaving it
as an unmet AC on an otherwise-complete ticket would either block that close or be silently
dropped.

## Observed impact

On 2026-09-05, **four changes across three sessions** were mislabelled as broken by 504s at
checkout. The cost is not just the wasted vote — it is that an author (human or agent) reads
`Verified -1`, opens the change, and starts debugging code that was never at fault. Two of tonight's
delegated investigations began exactly that way.

## Mechanism (verified in tree at 1f7673cb2c53)

Two places collapse the distinction:

1. **`.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:80-85`** — checkout runs through the third-party
   `checkout-gerrit-change-action`. A 504 there fails the job like any other step.
2. **`scripts/summarize_ci_failures.py:104-110`** — classifies outcomes as `TIMED OUT`,
   `CANCELLED (not a test verdict)`, or `FAILED`. There is no transport/infrastructure class, so a
   504 lands in `FAILED` and the voter casts `Verified -1`.

Note the file already draws exactly this distinction for **cancellation** — "not a test verdict" is
the concept, already present and already respected by the voter. This ticket extends that existing
seam to transport faults rather than inventing a new mechanism.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 A checkout/transport failure is classified distinctly from a test failure, reusing the
      existing "not a test verdict" seam in `scripts/summarize_ci_failures.py` rather than adding a
      parallel detection mechanism.
- [ ] AC2 On a transport failure the bot casts **no `Verified` vote** (leaving the change at 0,
      awaiting a real verdict) rather than `-1`. Justification: `-1` asserts the change is broken,
      which is a claim CI cannot support when it never ran the tests. The comment must say plainly
      that CI could not obtain the source and that this is not a statement about the change.
- [ ] AC3 The classifier is proven by a test that feeds it a real captured 504 checkout failure and
      asserts the transport class, plus a companion test feeding a genuine test failure and
      asserting it still classifies as `FAILED` and still votes `-1`. Both directions, so the fix
      cannot silently swallow real failures — that is the dangerous failure mode here, and it is
      strictly worse than the bug being fixed.
- [ ] AC4 A transport failure is **visible**, not silent: it is reported in the run summary and
      distinguishable at a glance, so a stalled change is not mistaken for one nobody has voted on
      yet.
- [ ] AC5 The detection does not depend on a specific CI provider's proprietary signal — it keys on
      the observable failure (HTTP status / git transport error text) so it remains portable to a
      different provider or none, per the blocking `project.portability` criterion.

## Explicitly out of scope

Retry-on-transport-failure. A retry is a *different* decision with its own risks (it can mask a
degrading edge and burn runner minutes), and conflating it with correct classification is how the
scope of this ticket would quietly triple. Classification first; any retry policy is a separate
ticket that can build on the class this one introduces.

## Constraints

Never use `--force` or any gate bypass. A flaky test is a bug to root-cause, never a retry;
`recheck` only for a provably environmental fault, stating that reasoning. `timeout` does not exist
on this macOS host (it exits 127, a silent no-op) — bound with `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'`. Do
not touch the shared main checkout; do not `git stash` anywhere.
data.title: CI votes Verified -1 on transport failures, mislabelling infrastructure faults as broken changes
